**Request changes.** The `forEach` change breaks the function's contract.

**1. Deletes are no longer awaited (serious)**

> `expired.forEach(async (s) => { await db.sessions.delete(s.id) })`

`forEach` ignores the promises its async callback returns, so `purgeExpired` returns before any delete has run. Any delete that rejects becomes an unhandled promise rejection, and the caller never sees the failure. The original `for...of` with `await` did not have this problem.

Fix: restore the sequential loop.

```js
for (const s of expired) await db.sessions.delete(s.id)
```

If you want parallel deletes, use `await Promise.all(expired.map((s) => db.sessions.delete(s.id)))`. That still rejects on the first failure, and it issues every delete at once, so use it only if the expired set is small or your DB handles the load.

**2. The log and return value report the wrong thing (moderate)**

> `console.log('purged', expired.length)`

This line runs before the deletes finish, so it logs how many sessions were found, not how many were purged. The same is true of `return { purged: expired.length }`. Once the deletes are awaited, the log and return value are accurate. If any delete can fail, count only the successful ones instead of using `expired.length`.
